page: Amazon Web Services i8g.48xlarge is a storage-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It is driven by 192 physical and virtual ARMv9 cores based on the AWS Neoverse-V2 microarchitecture running at 2.8 GHz with a single thread per dedicated core. The processor subsystem includes 64 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 36 MB L3 cache per socket structure. Memory resources total 1,536 GB, yielding an allocation of 8 GB per core. The server bundles 45,000 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and delivers a baseline network throughput of 100 Gbps. It does not include dedicated graphics processing hardware.

Performance profiles demonstrate high parallel compute efficiency. In multi-threaded evaluations, the server achieves top-tier ratings in stress-ng multi-core testing, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Clang compilation tasks. Memory subsystems deliver high transfer rates, exceeding 895 GB/sec in large uncached block reads and 411 GB/sec in uncached block writes. Storage and operational benchmarks reflect top-tier throughput in PassMark database tasks, static web serving, and Redis SET operations. Conversely, single-threaded metrics, including single-core stress-ng, Geekbench single-core, and small-model LLM prompt processing, fall within average to lower quartile ranges.

The instance delivers high cost efficiency when workloads leverage its massive local NVMe capacity and memory density, eliminating the overhead and transfer costs of remote network-attached volumes. The primary tradeoff lies in per-thread execution speed, which favors horizontal scale over raw single-core clock velocity. As a result, the platform is structured for large-scale database clusters, NoSQL datastores, distributed key-value caches, and high-throughput data ingestion pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services i8g.48xlarge is an arm64 storage-optimized instance built on the Nitro System. It integrates 192 dedicated AWS Neoverse-V2 ARMv9 physical cores operating at 2.8 GHz, paired with 1,536 GB of memory at an 8 GB per core ratio. Hardware capabilities include 45,000 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, a 100 Gbps baseline network interface, and no hardware GPUs. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier multi-threaded processing, leading database operation scores, and high Redis SET throughput, complemented by strong memory bandwidth across small and large blocks. Single-core performance and LLM prompt processing remain in the average to lower quartiles, reflecting an architecture focused on parallel throughput rather than individual core clock speed. By consolidating massive local storage and substantial RAM per core, this instance provides cost efficiency for high-density I/O deployments, making it well fitted for large-scale distributed databases, transactional systems, real-time caching, and data ingestion pipelines.
